extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator; literate early-18th-century public interested in manners, morals, and society
extracted.subtask_description: Short moral and social essays (The Spectator, early 18th century) offering judgments about virtue, behaviour, commerce, prizes and fashions, and practical advice on conduct. The pieces mix anecdote, moral reflection, and proposals for public improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value talents by their application to virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gifts of Nature and Accomplishments of Art are valuable, but as they are exerted in the Interest of Virtue, or governed by the Rules of Honour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not admire natural endowments (beauty, wit, skill) apart from how they are used; excellence should be appraised by whether it promotes what is good and honourable. Examples: painters/sculptors praised only for execution rather than moral purpose; talents misapplied become an injury to society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid admiring mere beauty or wit without judging disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to abstract our Minds from the Observation of any Excellence in those we converse with, till we have taken some Notice, or received some good Information of the Disposition of their Minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow reason and inquiry (light of Reason and Justice) to moderate initial fondness; outward charms may conceal vice and lead to 'abject Slavery' if unexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intention should be the measure of approbation
rubrics_metrics.description: Were the Intention stedfastly considered, as the Measure of Approbation, all Falsehood would soon be out of Countenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge actions and reputations by the agent's intent rather than only by skill or effect. Examples: eloquence used to defend unjust causes should not be admired as much as eloquence used for justice; resolution in an assassin is not truly laudable when contrasted with virtuous application of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve virtue and remain independent of public applause
rubrics_metrics.description: He only is a great Man who can neglect the Applause of the Multitude, and enjoy himself independent of its Favour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True glory is preserved by hearing opposers with patience and maintaining the virtue by which praise was earned; internal conviction of duty outranks public acclaim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes and competitions should promote useful handicraft improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Project of erecting several Handicraft Prizes ... and the Influence they might have towards the Improvement of our several Manufactures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitions and prizes are valuable when they stimulate the improvement of manufactures and useful arts; such incentives should be directed toward productive, improving ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid instituting or rewarding spectacles that affront human dignity
rubrics_metrics.description: A monstrous Tryal of Skill ... whether they are not guilty, in some measure, of an Affront to their Species, in treating after this manner the Human Face Divine, and turning that Part of us ... into the Image of a Monkey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contests that celebrate deformity, ridicule, or gratuitous grotesquery (e.g., grinning matches, ass-races) are immoral and ridiculous and should not be encouraged or patronised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold fairness in competitions; disqualify artificial aids or cheats
rubrics_metrics.description: He had practised with Verjuice for some Days before, and had a Crab found upon him ... the best Judges of Grinning declared it as their Opinion, that he was not to be looked upon as a fair Grinner, and therefore ordered him to be set aside as a Cheat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges should enforce rules prohibiting artificial enhancement or deceit; fairness and authenticity of performance are grounds for disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use numbers and accounting as the measure of prudence in commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers are so much the Measure of every thing that is valuable, that it is not possible to demonstrate the Success of any Action, or the Prudence of any Undertaking, without them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before undertaking trade or ventures, compute demand, customary prices, cargo charges, freight, insurance, customs, interest, and expected profit. Prudence and justification of an adventure require numeric calculation and reasonable presumption of returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect merchants' contributions: industry and accounts create social value
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Preparation of his Cargo and the Manufacture of his Returns, he furnishes Employment and Subsistence to greater Numbers than the richest Nobleman; and even the Nobleman is obliged to him for finding out foreign Markets for the Produce of his Estate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess economic actors by the practical benefits they create (employment, markets) rather than by social prejudice; careful accounting and enterprise are socially useful and deserving of esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit from industry outweighs inherited negligence
rubrics_metrics.description: He deserves the Estate a great deal better, who has got it by his Industry, than he who has lost it by his Negligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social approbation should favor those who acquire position through diligent, prudent industry rather than those preserving status by neglect; this justifies social mobility through commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid envy caused by comparing one’s condition with another’s
rubrics_metrics.description: There was a secret, tho' unjust, Way among Men, of indulging the Seeds of ill Nature and Envy, by comparing their own State of Life to that of another, and grudging the Approach of their Neighbour to their own Happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that comparative judgment breeds ill-nature across professions and ranks (civil vs military, tradesmen vs landed gentry); cultivate contentment and avoid petty rivalries that harm social harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess both your companions and yourself before engaging in wit or raillery
rubrics_metrics.description: The best Rule I can lay down for them to avoid the like Calamities for the future, is thoroughly to consider not only Whether their Companions are weak, but Whether themselves are Wits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before attempting repartee or public raillery, evaluate opponents' temper and your own ability; being mismatched leads to embarrassment or loss of reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central inspection of fashions (proposed standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: That there may be a Society erected in London ... for the Inspection of Modes and Fashions; and that hereafter no Person ... shall presume to appear singularly habited in any Part of the Country, without a Testimonial ... that their Dress is answerable to the Mode at London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal (satirical/serious) to regulate provincial fashions by a London authority so country people can be sure they conform to metropolitan standards; intended as a civic remedy for false 'London fashions' exported to the country.
